findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security
Case: normal use - a task review reports an authorization defect as `Not done: Orders are scoped to their owner` with a security category or raise. The new exception retains the finding, but `src/forge/review.py:1102` still marks it as a follow-up because its title does not match a covered item. `src/forge/score.py:132` then prevents it from blocking, and `src/forge/worker.py:545` excludes it from the builder's brief. A review containing only this security finding can therefore be reported clean; the new test misses this because another finding blocks the close.

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security
Case: normal use - a task review reports a low-score advisory on one handler and a P0 authorization defect on another handler in the same file, both with the same title; the repair review repeats the P0. This key now retains both findings, but `src/forge/review.py:632` records the advisory as known using only the file and title. The carried dismissal at `src/forge/review.py:1040` then applies that settlement to the distinct P0 as well. The unfixed security finding no longer blocks the repair review or reaches the next builder.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a first review contains a real blocking finding, a duplicate, and a builder-guidance note. The revised proof checks the saved state and review event, but it still never runs `forge work` or inspects the brief sent to the worker. A regression that reintroduces the duplicate or guidance while assembling that brief would pass this test, so the named proof still does not check the required builder-facing boundary.
